text: Nuclear power is the fastest scalable path to deep decarbonization, and any climate plan that excludes it is not serious. France decarbonized most of its electricity in under two decades by building standardized reactors, a feat no country has matched with wind and solar alone. Critics reply that new plants routinely run about a decade late and billions over budget, which makes renewables the cheaper marginal investment. Decarbonization, properly understood, means cutting total system emissions, not merely adding low-carbon supply. Governments should therefore extend the lifetimes of existing reactors while the cost question for new construction is settled in the open.
